notes:
I couldn't research Psalm 78:49–72, so I have no notes for you. My research tool was blocked on the first try, before it opened any pages, and it was blocked again when I retried. That means I haven't read anything from Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, the NET Bible or the other sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything from memory. Notes without sources would break both of those rules.

If you ask again in a new turn, my access to the tool may be restored, and I'll start over. I plan to read these pages first:
- **Verse-by-verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-78/ and the Bible Hub pages for each verse, such as biblehub.com/commentaries/psalms/78-60.htm. Those pages carry Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and others. Then StudyLight and Precept Austin.
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on Psalm 78, and Bible Odyssey on Shiloh and on why God chose Judah and Zion over Ephraim.
- **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (for v. 65, "awoke as from sleep," and vv. 70–72 on David as a picture of Christ), Wesley's notes, and Gill (Baptist). For Reformed views I'll check Ligonier, Monergism and TGC, and for Lutheran views LCMS and 1517.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's commentary on Psalm 78 on New Advent, which is Psalm 77 in his numbering.

You could also paste in text from any of these pages, and I'll write the verse-by-verse notes using only what's in that text.
